newsitem.title: USA: Weston wins Army restoration contract.
newsitem.headline: Weston wins Army restoration contract.

text.p: Roy F. Weston Inc said Wednesday it won a $13.6 million contract from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers for environmental restoration of the former Weldon Spring Ordnance Works in Weldon Spring, Missouri.
Work for the contract will begin in July and is expected to be completed in December 1998, the company said.
The contract brings the total value of Weston's thermal treatment work for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to $75 million in the past five years, Weston said.

Weston said its work at Weldon Spring would involve excavation of 30,000 cubic yards of materials contaminated with heavy metals and explosives, thermal treatment of 18,500 cubic yards of soil contaminated with explosives and chemical fixation of 9,000 cubic yards of soil contaminated with heavy metals.
The company said it would also remove 85,000 linear feet of wooden sewer lines previously used to convey wastewater. It will thermally treat the wastewater for on-site reuse, it said.
